units.name: Introduction
units.assessment: Can you say what separates chronic lymphocytic leukemia from small lymphocytic lymphoma and from monoclonal B lymphocytosis when the flow cytometry phenotype is identical in all three?

lesson.title: Diagnosis and Management of Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia
lesson.why: A journal-produced review that covers definition, workup and current treatment in under twenty minutes, which is the right orientation for the chapter opener.

units.name: Epidemiology
units.assessment: Can you describe how CLL incidence varies with age, sex and ancestry, and quantify roughly how much risk a first-degree relative with CLL carries compared with the background population?

lesson.title: The epidemiology of CLL: What do we know about risk?
lesson.why: Devoted entirely to who gets CLL and why - incidence, age distribution and the epidemiologic risk signal - which is what this short section asks for.

units.name: Biology
units.assessment: Can you explain why dependence on B-cell receptor signaling and on BCL2 makes CLL cells vulnerable to BTK and BCL2 inhibition, and rank del(13q), trisomy 12, del(11q) and del(17p) by biology rather than by memory?

lesson.title: Causes and Consequences of Genetic Abnormalities in Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia
lesson.why: An academic talk on the genetic lesions of CLL and what each of them does to the cell, which is the mechanistic core of this section.

units.name: Diagnosis and clinical evaluation
units.assessment: Given persistent lymphocytosis, can you list the flow-cytometry markers that define the CLL immunophenotype, state the absolute B-cell threshold the iwCLL criteria require, and say when a marrow biopsy actually adds information?

lesson.title: Provider Connections: Dr. Neil Kay on Newly Diagnosed Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia, Watch and Wait
lesson.why: A 2026 clinician-to-clinician conversation about how a newly diagnosed patient is evaluated and why most are observed rather than treated.

units.assessment: Can you name the four variables in the CLL-IPI and explain why TP53 aberration and IGHV mutation status are rechecked before each line of therapy rather than measured once at diagnosis?

lesson.title: The Risk-Stratifying Factors in CLL
lesson.why: Runs through the individual risk-stratifying factors - stage, IGHV, FISH, TP53, beta-2 microglobulin - and how they combine into a prognostic index.

units.assessment: Can you state the iwCLL indications for starting treatment rather than observing, and argue the case for continuous BTK inhibition versus fixed-duration venetoclax plus obinutuzumab in a fit patient with mutated IGHV?

lesson.why: A 2025 practice-focused discussion with a CLL specialist covering when to treat and how covalent BTK inhibitors and fixed-duration venetoclax are chosen between.
